SRC-289:R001.text: Sections 0, 19: use canonical START and genuine host ingress; preserve the entire original request and honest original provenance. Never forge authority, reset hard_wait without trusted input, substitute persisted work, or cross a real admission or approval boundary.

SRC-289:R002.text: Sections 1, 6: measure the live canonical state, dependency topology, source sizes and all five unchanged context budgets; distinguish historical snapshots from current evidence and separate context, code and storage metrics.

SRC-289:R003.text: Sections 2, 3: one canonical machine-readable blocker projection exposes class, root cause, owner, shared identity, dependent IDs, internal recovery authority, external-input need, read-only eligibility, exact recovery operation and safe-resumption preconditions. Group the shared publication obstruction without erasing tickets or edges.

SRC-289:R004.text: Section 3: retain registered verdict semantics and distinguish all work complete, no runnable work, operator wait, external wait, recoverable blockers and unsafe continuation. 102 blocked plus three dependent TODO items must never imply completion; display the immediate actionable shared obstruction while preserving older Work.

SRC-289:R005.text: Section 4: inspect release scope, foreign staging, index capture and ownership, journal recovery, preflight and attribution. Preserve every existing strict protection; do not reset, stash, add all, clear or commit foreign staging, force-push, rewrite branches or replace history.

SRC-289:R006.text: Section 4: prove a canonical isolated publication mechanism commits only the exact reviewed source generation, preserves live index and foreign entries byte-for-byte and worktree contents, ancestry, history, evidence identity, concurrency safety and crash recovery. Use adversarial staged-file fixtures and executed red-before-green controls; explicitly amend and test the release contract if required, otherwise retain the refusal and exact missing operator action.

SRC-289:R007.text: Sections 5, 7: recursively remove proven duplicate knowledge and decisions through one authoritative owner, caller and contract maps, equivalence tests, redirected callers, dead-code removal and before/after measurements. Preserve all qualifications, errors, semantics and capabilities; never substitute physical archive compression or obscured side effects for simpler architecture.

SRC-289:R008.text: Section 8: build a rule-ownership graph across the named registry, protocol owners and phase documents; classify normative, derived, explanatory, compatibility, contradictory and obsolete occurrences. Each normative rule has one owner; preserve Rule IDs, observable meaning, conditional loads and acyclic references; measure actual loaded surfaces.

SRC-289:R009.text: Section 9: consolidate executable command, compound-order, admission, authority, lifecycle, blocker, response, HUSH, verification and publication facts into existing machine owners and schemas. Derive compatible runtime, validator, documentation and regression projections without another registry.

SRC-289:R010.text: Sections 9, 17: reuse existing T-1853, T-1854 and T-1855 Work and acceptance contracts; do not create competing implementations or duplicate tickets for their requirements.

SRC-289:R011.text: Section 10: inspect actual ownership in the listed engine modules and narrowly consolidate equivalent validation, transaction preparation, BOARD/registry reads, source and authority checks, classifications, hashes, Git probes, projections, recovery and repeated validation. Move cohesive subsystems with API/data parity and explicit safety.

SRC-289:R012.text: Section 11: classify active state, immutable evidence, derived indexes, disposable cache and historical archive from contracts. Investigate repeated snapshots, reports, outputs, indexes and serialization; do not delete evidence. Any dedupe or migration preserves hashes, attribution, references, exact reconstruction, rollback, old-reader compatibility and crash/partial-migration safety.

SRC-289:R013.text: Section 12: reduce actual conditional context loads using complete bounded canonical projections, never model memory. Measure every profile before and after; target at least 25 percent cold and 30 percent ordinary-phase and command-resolution reductions plus fewer rereads. Preserve all mandatory semantic dependencies and existing budget limits; report unmet targets honestly.

SRC-289:R014.text: Section 13: preserve test-cost-collapse mechanisms, STATIC/FOCUSED/IMPACT/FULL scope, single-flight and compatible evidence reuse. Never trust stale identities, fabricate PASS or weaken SHIP; run full evidence on a stable generation when required and measure comparable invocation counts, reuse, wall time and regressions.

SRC-289:R015.text: Section 14: maintain a semantic preservation map of old/new owner, original Rule ID, callers, preserved contract and regression evidence for every consolidation. Cover all listed authority, ownership, transactions, recovery, replay, sources, lifecycle, publication, verification, host, historical, concurrency, refusal and confirmation boundaries with valid, hostile and controlled golden comparisons.

SRC-289:R016.text: Section 15: demonstrate every adversarial control A-T: honest idle, fresh ingress, grouped and prioritized blockers, dependency safety, independent work, foreign staging and reviewed scope, absent authority and invalid receipts, malformed state, compatible versus stale PASS, valid workflows, evidence discovery, host privilege limits, interruption safety, complete projections, acyclic rule ownership and no fabricated progress.

SRC-289:R017.text: Section 16: use bounded read-only connectivity checks for T-1829 original-object integrity; distinguish GitHub access, backup availability, history, source publication and release authority. Recover only trustworthy original objects; never synthesize commits, force-push or repeatedly probe the unchanged frontier.

SRC-289:R018.text: Section 17: execute bounded waves W0-W10 in measured dependency order, preserving evidence, metrics and canonical transitions; re-evaluate admissible work and continue independent authorized waves when one blocks. Admit meaningful new Work with real sources and avoid campaign-wide artificial dependency chains.

SRC-289:R019.text: Section 18: before expensive operations identify the decision, existing evidence, generation and expected cost; prefer focused checks and eliminate repeated self-audits and executions. Measure context, boundaries, branches, reads, processed bytes, startup/routing/continuation latency, test time, storage and recovery behavior rather than line count alone.

SRC-289:R020.text: Section 19: stop product mutation at genuine authority, approval, identity, ownership, index-safety, irreversible-action or environment boundaries; preserve all work/evidence, identify the exact blocker and owner, and never disguise refusal as completion or ask the operator to do routine safe diagnosis.

SRC-289:R021.text: Section 20: preserve per-wave STATUS, ROOT CAUSE, CHANGED COMPONENTS, RULES CONSOLIDATED, BEFORE/AFTER MEASUREMENTS, VERIFICATION, SEMANTIC PARITY, SAFETY REGRESSIONS and NEXT EXACT ACTION. Track every requested campaign total, actual completed Work, regressions and remaining external blockers without invented percentages or premature completion.

SRC-289:R022.text: Section 21: prove the full campaign yields smaller required context, simpler execution, cheaper verification, faster continuation, clearer blockers and maintainability with no security, correctness or recovery loss. Preserve distinctions among absent, blocked, authority-limited, recoverable and independently executable work; one shortened document cannot discharge this mission.
